idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the latest deploy to v2.3.1 (all three production regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west; error rate ~18%). v2.3.1 was marked unhealthy in the release history (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy). Remedi ation: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed-version fleet (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback completed successfully, and all production regions are now on v2.3.0. Post-rollback status: healthy=true, error rate down to ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the orchestrator/rollout failure that caused the partial rollout, and determine why v2.3.1 passed pre-production checks but failed health checks in production before any re-deploy attempt.
args.title: checkout-api: health-check failures on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions

trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

**Rollback: checkout-api v2.3.1 → v2.3.0**
- Deployment history showed v2.3.1 (current, unhealthy) and v2.3.0 as the most recent release with a **healthy production** record. v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so v2.3.0 was the correct target.
- **First rollback attempt failed partially**: `partial_failure` — rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed fleet (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1).
- I re-checked status to confirm the partial state, then **retried the rollback**, which completed: all three production regions now on v2.3.0.
- **Verified:** `healthy: true`, error rate dropped from ~18% to ~0.2%.

**Incident: INC-0001 (SEV2, open, on-call paged)**
- Describes the v2.3.1 health-check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the halted-then-retried rollout.
- The first create call timed out client-side, so I retried with the **same idempotency key**; `list_incidents` confirms exactly one incident exists — no duplicate page.

**Two things worth flagging for follow-up** (both noted in the incident):
1. The orchestrator error that halted the rollout mid-way is unexplained — worth investigating, since a partial rollback left two regions on a bad version for longer than necessary.
2. INC-0001's summary text rendered with a minor typo from the timed-out first request ("Remedi ation"). The content is accurate but I have no tool to edit it — someone may want to correct that in the incident record.

Also note: no approval was required here since rollback targets a version with a prior healthy production record; the change-manager approval gate applies to deploying a never-healthy version, which I did not do.
